condition.narrative: On-lending to PFIs shall be made only in accordance with the Eligibility Criteria, Terms and Conditions listed in Loan Agreement.

Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Loan AgreementThe Borrower shall, throughout the implementation of the Project, maintain itsProject Implementation Unit and ensure that said unit functions at all times in a manner and with staffing and budgetary resourcesnecessary and appropriate for implementation of the Project and satisfactory to the Bank.Effectiveness ConditionSection 6.01 ofthe Loan AgreementThe Borrower shall have adopted a revised Operational Manual satisfactory to the Bank.
Sub-financing to SMEs shall be made only in accordance with the Eligibility Criteria, Terms, Conditions and Approval Procedureslisted in Loan Agreement.

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Financial Sustainability: Return on Assets (%)
Based on Core Indicator: Financial Sustainability: Return on Assets (%)

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator's purpose was to monitor the borrower's profitability (which was generating losses at the start of the project). The borrowers reported a strong increase in net profit in the last year of implementation, mainly due to the recovery of loan portfolio quality and favorable monetary policy (high interest rate environment). </p>

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Financial Sustainability: Return on Equity (%)
Based on Core Indicator: Financial Sustainability: Return on Equity (%)

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator's purpose was to monitor the borrower's profitability (which was generating losses at the start of the project). The borrowers reported a strong increase in net profit in the last year of implementation, mainly due to the recovery of loan portfolio quality and favorable monetary policy (high interest rate environment). </p>

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Portfolio Quality: Portfolio at risk (%).

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator's purpose was to monitor the quality of the borrower's overall loan portfolio. It has shown significant positive progress due to actions of the borrower to resolve legacy NPLS, including through restructurings, resolution, and write-off (many of these actions were enabled by the paralell World Bank support through DPO operations).  </p>

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Portfolio Quality: Portfolio at risk (%).

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. UEB has been compliant with NBU prudential requirements for most of the project's lifetime. However, unprecedented challenges  impacted asset quality and caused losses on UEB, forcing it to fall out of compliance with several prudential ratios and later by the unexpected introduction of a one-off bank windfall profit tax of 50 percent at end 2023. These required issuing three waivers on UEB's compliance with the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) prudential requirements. In 2023, UEB earned strong net income, however, the delay in hiring the new external auditor postponed recognition of the retained earnings for 2023 into the bank capital, after which it can potentially reach its prudential capital requirements. </p>

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Volume of Bank Support: Lines of Credit - SME (cumulative, USD million).
Based on Core Indicator: Volume of Bank Support: Lines of Credit - SME (cumulative, USD million).

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved. As explained th the text of this report, while the project has been fully disbursed by the World Bank (including the designated account of the borrowers), UEB notified the World Bank that US$13.9 million in approved loans could not be disbursed to sub-borrowers at a time of project closure due to the restrictions imposed on the bank by the NBU for the failure of the bank to meet the prudential ratio on large exposure, which is related to the delay in completing the audit. For this purpose, the extension of the last disbursement date to 30 June 2024 was provided to UEB to complete the disbursement of these approved projects. As of completing this report, it was not known which of this outstanding amount UEB managed to disburse to sub-borrowers.  </p>

title.narrative: Number of active PFIs under the project (cumulative).

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The intermediate indicator related to a cumulative number of PFIs, with which UEB has signed a subsidiary financing agreement, reached the target of three. However, only two of them have disbursed to SMEs, and one subsidiary agreement expired undisbursed. The minimal number of PFIs is explained by the limited ability of UEB to attract new PFIs during the martial law as the NBU’s forbearance measures were introduced, whereby UEB could not accept new PFIs given newly introduced exposure limits to other banks and the inability to assess PFIs' performance in line with the project requirements. Pre-war PFIs were also reluctant to borrow the project funds in US$, given the low interest rate on FX liquidity and the limited availability of FX hedge options. </p>

Number of SME beneficiaries financed by PFIs under the project (cumulative).

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved. The targeted number of borrowers was not reached due to extraordinary circumstances and the limited ability of UEB to attract new clients and participating banks due to martial law. UEB was given a waiver for the slower-than-expected. </p>

title.narrative: Gender: Percent of SME beneficiaries financed under the project with at least 15 percent female participation in their workforce.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The share of SME beneficiaries financed under the project with at least 15 percent female participation in their workforce was near 90% at project closure, and in some periods of project implementation, this share exceeded 90%. </p>

title.narrative: Citizen Engagement: SMEs that report that project sub-finance reflected their needs.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. In October-November 2023, UEB, jointly with the WB team, conducted a Citizen Engagement survey to collect feedback from the SME beneficiaries on their satisfaction with the sub-financing. The detailed results of the survey are presented in Annex 4 of this ICR.</p>

title.narrative: Citizen Engagement: SMEs that report that project sub-finance reflected their needs.

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The export-oriented small and medium enterprises were able to obtain longer-term funding under the project, with the average maturity of the project portfolio more than 20% the average maturity of the SME loan portfolio outside of the project.  </p>

Based on Core Indicator: Outstanding SME finance portfolio (USD million).
Based on Core Indicator: Outstanding SME finance portfolio (USD million).

comment.narrative: <p>The purpose of the indicator was to monitor the dynamic of the overall SME loan portfolio of the borrower (including those issued outside of the project). The indicator was severely impacted by powerful exogenous factors in the course of implementation, which had a devastating impact on the SMEs through distractions of physical assets and infrastructure, loss of life, and reduction in labor force, lack of energy resources, blackouts, broken logistic ways, among other, significantly limited the ability of almost 80 percent of the firms to increase their production capacity and take additional loans.  </p>

title.narrative: Based on Core Indicator: Number of active SME finance accounts (not cumulative).

comment.narrative: <p>The purpose of the indicator was to monitor the dynamic of the number of overall SME clients of the borrower (including those issued outside of the project). The indicator was negatively impacted by powerful exogenous factors in the course of implementation. </p>

Share of the volume of financing provided to sub-borrowers with less than 250 employees
Share of the volume of financing provided to sub-borrowers with less than 250 employees

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced to monitor the lending to smaller SMEs under the projects, given that for the purposes of the project, the definition of an SME was expanded to include enterprises with staff headcount below 1,000, which was explained by the labor-intensive economy of Ukraine.</p>

title.narrative: Share of female-led SMEs (i.e. have Director/CEO, Deputy/member of the Management Board, Chief Accountant/CFO or woman owning >50% stake or is the sole proprietor)
Share of female-led SMEs (i.e. have Director/CEO, Deputy/member of the Management Board, Chief Accountant/CFO or woman owning >50% stake or is the sole proprietor)

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target. 83.5% of sub-borrowers under the project were led by a female Director/CEO, Deputy/member of the Management Board, Chief Accountant/CFO, or woman owning >50% stake. The increased role of women in the management of companies can be partially explained by the current circumstances.</p>
